# Now 2.13.19
- Instrumental breaks are now a real part of the lyric script, like Apple Music: the interlude dots have a fixed place in the timeline, sit dimmed in the scroll so you can see a break coming, and light up left-to-right as a countdown to the next line — instead of popping in and out of the middle of the lyrics. - Smoother lyric motion: the scroll and the line emphasis now share a single spring, so the whole column moves as one coordinated gesture, and the per-line animation overhead was consolidated. No change to resource usage.

# Now 2.13.18
- Smoother lyric scrolling: the full-screen lyric list now lays out eagerly, so the line-change animation lands on a stable target instead of occasionally hitching while off-screen lines were built mid-scroll. No change to resource usage. - Instrumental gaps now show animated dots (like Apple Music) instead of holding the last line lit — during a long intro, an interlude between lines, or the outro. The dots animate on their own without any added CPU cost, and appear only when there's a genuine pause in the vocals.

# Now 2.13.17
- Lower CPU while lyrics play: the karaoke word-sweep now redraws at 12 Hz instead of 20 Hz. This is the single biggest cost in the full-screen view (re-rendering the active line's text), so this cuts it by roughly 40% while staying visually smooth.
